model.initial_state: promotion P is PREPARED; shard A holds reservation P/A; shard B is unreserved; abort is requested before global COMMIT

release_before_abort_reacquire_window.definition: old A writer reacquires after A release while intent is still PREPARED; no stale coordinator/new promotion/rate limit; response observed; terminal witness kept; GC target varies
release_before_abort_reacquire_window.release_then_abort: 3/3 post-abort resurrection; terminal ABORTED exists later but the release step has already passed, so the reacquired P reservation is stranded
release_before_abort_reacquire_window.abort_then_release_name_only: 0 resurrection in this slice because ABORTED is visible before the late writer

response_lost_then_target_reuse.definition: no late/stale writer; A release actually applies but response is lost; new promotion acquires A; blind release retry occurs; GC then targets A
response_lost_then_target_reuse.cleanup_by_delete: stale retry deletes the new reservation and GC deletes the newly-live root
response_lost_then_target_reuse.abort_then_release_name_only: same stale-release/live-GC failure despite correct abort ordering because release is name-only
response_lost_then_target_reuse.monotonic_abort_epoch_release: 0 stale release and 0 live-root deletion: readback/exact reservation epoch detects that P/A is gone and never deletes the new epoch

terminal_witness_deleted_then_stale_B.definition: B late writer + stale coordinator, no new promotion/rate limit, observed A release; bulky/terminal intent is deleted after abort; GC target varies
terminal_witness_deleted_then_stale_B.release_then_abort: 3/3 resurrection + 3/3 orphan after terminal record deletion
terminal_witness_deleted_then_stale_B.abort_then_release_name_only: 3/3 resurrection + 3/3 orphan after terminal record deletion
terminal_witness_deleted_then_stale_B.monotonic_abort_epoch_release: 0 resurrection/orphan because deleting bulky intent retains a compact terminal promotion-id/epoch witness

scope_safe_conclusion.ordering_rule: Abort must become a monotonic current authority state before releasing shard reservations. Release-first creates a window where old PREPARED writers can reacquire and survive the later abort.
scope_safe_conclusion.release_identity_rule: Shard cleanup must compare exact promotion_id + reservation epoch/incarnation. Name/path-only release is unsafe under ambiguous response plus target reuse because a retry can delete the next promotion's reservation.
scope_safe_conclusion.terminal_retention_rule: Deleting the only ABORTED witness reopens old-writer ambiguity. Bulky intent may be compacted only if a compact terminal promotion-id/epoch witness remains in the same authority domain consulted by late writers and cleanup.
scope_safe_conclusion.candidate: CAS intent PREPARED->ABORTED monotonically under current coordinator epoch; every late bridge must prove current PREPARED so it is rejected after ABORTED; release each shard only when current reservation matches exact promotion_id+reservation_epoch; ambiguous release response is read-before-retry; new promotion uses a new reservation epoch; GC proceeds only from current shard root/reservation state. Persistent rate limit may leave an ABORTED-but-cleanup-pending reservation, which is recoverable/nonterminal rather than orphaned.
not_proven: The strong candidate retains a compact terminal witness; safe GC of that witness is the next child.
Rate-limited release can cause conservative blockage until cleanup resumes; wait-free progress is not claimed.
Complete repository rollback that erases terminal witness and shard epochs remains unresolved.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport: role-local monotonic intent + shard reservation CAS/readback only

frontier: Terminal promotion witness compaction: determine when ABORTED/COMMITTED promotion IDs and shard reservation epochs can be compacted without allowing old bridge/release replay after later target reuse.
Adaptive shard split/merge while an ABORTED cleanup-pending reservation exists.
Bounded retention index to avoid one tombstone per promotion while preserving a monotonic lower bound against old epochs.
exact_continuation: Model terminal promotion-witness compaction. Compare delete-all-terminal-records, per-promotion tombstone, per-target minimum-reservation-epoch watermark, per-shard monotonic promotion generation floor, and fail-closed. Adversaries: very late old bridge/release, new target incarnation, shard split/merge, restore/replay of old checkpoint, response loss, watermark update lag, and rate-limit interruption. Measure old-writer acceptance, stale release of new reservation, retained-state growth, false blockage, and recovery reads.
